title.narrative: The efficiency and effectiveness of the design and implementation of EDF programmes are increased and sustained.

description.narrative: Limited actions undertaken by KE2 on strengthening NAOSU systems, however slow progress due to absence of TATLProgramming, Identification & Formulation of 11th EDF & 12th EDF:WaSH Part 1 TORs for 3 FWCs prepared by NAOSU / TA team to support WaSH governance and strengthen WaSH sector.WASH Part2Dialogue with EUD, Water PNG and NAOSU failed; EUD made unilateral decision to delegate project implementation to UNICEF and UNOPS.FS3 (Policy Reform and Good Governance) EUDinitiated and led consultations with Ministries of Justiceand Police;Supported discussions leading to the formulation of Covid19 log frame for STREIT projectParticipated in STREIT project stakeholder consultation meetingMonitoring & Coordination of 10th & 11th projects:FS.1 (Rural Entrepreneurship,Investment & Trade) Ongoing dialogue with implementing partners on the inception phase of theprogramme. The inception plan presented by FAO during the PSC meeting of 10 February2020 was discussed virtually to monitor the status of the project. On the 4th of June 2020, the 1st Taskforce force meeting to place. The objective of the taskforce is to ensure that the project delivers outputs and outcomes that contributes to the achievement of the targets set under the relevant sectors, as stated in the MTDP3. Secondly, to promote the efficient and effective implementation of the project through facilitation and support from the relevant GoPNG stakeholder agencies, and thirdly, to ensure broad ownership of the project and its outcomes by stakeholders and the Taskforce. Drafted TORs for an assessment of the impact of the SoE on the three value chains and feasibility study on the establishment of a public commodity trading facility at the PNGIndonesia Wutugn BorderFS.2 (WASH Pt.1) Ongoing coordination with EUD, UNICEF, WASH PMU on the implementation of the programme. A workshop on WASH1 logical framework was held with the WASH PMU to identify possible TA support requirements (Eur 1,5m). WaSH Part 1 Monitoring Site inspections Morobe Three framework contracts concluded for (i) Capacity Building of the WASH PMU and the NationalService Delivery Framework, (ii) Development of WASH Technical Standards and Guidelines; and (iii) Rollout of mWater as the National M&E Tool for WASH. The selection of experts were done unilaterally by EU and did not involve the NAOSU nor the WASH PMU. The WaSH PMU Coordinator raised strong objections on the selection process and rejected the selection of the Team Leader; these objections received strong support from the Secretary DNPM and DNAO. Although all parties agreed to a homebased inception phase, the issue of the selection process and the objections raised by the WaSH PMU coordinator and DNAO appear yet to be resolved.Existing 10th EDF programmes (HRDP1, HRDP2, TRA2, RED1, RED2,and Regional Cooperation);HRDP.2 The implementation period of the project ended in March except for the infrastructure component which ended in August 2020. The NAOSU with the Supervisor of Works carried out monitoring and inspection visits to the 10 sites to assess the completion status of theproject and to allow the issuance of Provisional Acceptance Certificate. Support continued to be provided DoE in the final phase of the project most, particularly on the followingcomponents. Infrastructure Tools & Equipment Supported the Department of Education with the final audit of the PE.RED.1 Following the final evaluation of RED1 and 2 which took place on the 1720 March 2020, the NAOSU continued to provide feedback to the evaluator as the mission had to be suspended midway due to the first lockdown because of covid19
